title: The Bitter Lesson
unplayable_reason: The essay makes a historical, qualitative argument: knowledge-based methods help early but plateau, while search and learning keep scaling as Moore's law makes computation cheaper. It gives these as observations from chess, Go, speech and vision. It states no equations, functional forms, rates or worked numbers. There is no performance-versus-compute curve, no plateau level, no growth rate and no crossover point. A figure would have to invent the dynamics, so its output would be my assumptions rather than anything the document says. An honest diagram also has nothing to compute from the text alone, so there is no fallback.
